# visual-metronome

**Level:** Serial commands. No AI subscription or API key is needed.

[Start here](https://mikersays.github.io/agent-arduino/getting-started.html) · [Website instructions](https://mikersays.github.io/agent-arduino/sketches.html#visual-metronome) · [All sketches](../README.md)

## What you should see

A dot swings at 100 beats per minute in groups of four, with a brighter first beat. This is a silent visual metronome.

## What you need

No external components; uses the built-in LEDs or matrix.

Install Arduino_RouterBridge with Library Manager. The UNO Q core supplies the board-specific headers.

## Upload this sketch

1. Complete the getting-started guide once to install the UNO Q core and libraries.
2. In Arduino IDE, open visual-metronome/visual-metronome.ino. Select Arduino UNO Q and its port.
3. Click Verify, then Upload. Uploading replaces the running microcontroller sketch.

Or, in the **UNO Q Linux terminal**, from the repository root:

```bash
python3 flash visual-metronome
```

Read the replacement prompt and enter `y` to compile and upload. To check compilation without uploading:

```bash
python3 flash visual-metronome --compile-only
```

The helper uploads locally on the board. For a computer-side IDE or network CLI upload, follow the getting-started guide.

## Try it

Send BPM 60 and TS 3. Expect one beat per second, grouped in threes. STOP freezes it; START resumes it.

## Send commands

Follow [the serial monitor setup](https://mikersays.github.io/agent-arduino/getting-started.html#serial): 115200 baud, newline ending, one command per line. Values in angle brackets describe what to enter; do not type the brackets. A slash separates alternatives.

- `BPM <40-240>` — beats per minute
- `TS <2-7>` — beats per bar
- `TAP` — send repeatedly in time to set tempo
- `START / STOP` — run or freeze
- `STATUS` — report settings

Serial input still needs end-to-end verification. Settings are held in memory and reset when the sketch restarts.

## If it does not work

Compare the result with the expected behavior above, then follow [troubleshooting](https://mikersays.github.io/agent-arduino/getting-started.html#troubleshooting). Save your edits before downloading or uploading another version.

The repository records compilation with UNO Q core 0.56.0 on the original board. Typed serial input and most visual behavior still need hardware verification. These instructions describe the source code, not a new hardware test.

[Read the source](visual-metronome.ino) for the implementation and its original compile/upload commands.
